quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in areas outside cities and villages when no speed limit is posted?

options.text: 25 mph
35 mph
45 mph
None of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in areas outside cities and villages is 35 mph when no other speed limit is posted.

questions.question: When visibility gets worse, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Reducing your speed is the first thing you should do when visibility gets worse and road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect how far a vehicle takes to stop?

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection ahead.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you about an upcoming curve to the right.

questions.question: How far can a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph take to stop?

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers take much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer can take about 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
An intersection is ahead.
A four-way stop is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
A parking area is ahead.
A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Get out and walk to the back of your car to check if the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk to the back of your car to check if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out of the vehicle and check behind it before backing up, especially when children are nearby. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down as you exit the interstate?

options.text: Halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to match the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When passing another car, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space to return to your lane safely. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, there is enough space between you.

questions.question: When turning left from a multi-lane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multi-lane streets and highways.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake gently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake gently.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes or make sharp turns in bad weather. Gentle steering and braking help you control your vehicle better.

questions.question: How should you position your hands on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
One at the top and one at the bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and safe for turning on high-speed roads.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check your blind spots before you change lanes.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
Only during daylight hours.
Anytime.
When making a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making a turn.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can cross a solid yellow line only when you are turning.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Leave less space between you and the car ahead.
Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden speed changes or sharp turns on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat and pushing your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is unsafe.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is unsafe.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: You are approaching a traffic light showing steady yellow. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass before the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: At a yellow light, stop your vehicle safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue at a safe speed.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. These signs control traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking. They are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what speed should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: About how many alcoholic drinks does your body process in one hour?

options.text: Three drinks.
One drink.
Two drinks.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink.
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one drink per hour on average. How impaired you become depends on many factors, including how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, whether you ate, and your health.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again in case you missed any vehicles.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: A green arrow changes to a solid green light. What can you do?

options.text: You may turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You do not have to turn anymore.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check freeway traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic on the freeway before you merge.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Do not go until the intersection is clear and it is safe to pass through.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
In the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle. This keeps you away from both dangers.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
Always stop.
Divided highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: On an interstate, what is the best way to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: On interstate highways, watch for on-ramps. When it is safe, move to the left lane. This gives vehicles room to enter from the on-ramp on your right.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look at the bright headlights of an oncoming car. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road. Then look ahead to see where the other car is.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you remember?

options.text: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke ahead on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down immediately. Move as far right as you can and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or health.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when passing a bicycle. The cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Drive extra carefully near bicycles.

questions.question: On a road with two lanes going the same direction, which lane should you drive in?

options.text: The left lane to avoid vehicles entering from the right.
The right lane only when you plan to exit.
The left lane except to pass.
The right lane except to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane except to pass.
questions.explanation: On a road with two or more lanes going the same direction, stay in the right lane except when passing. On a road with three or more lanes, stay as far right as possible.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances to drivers.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show directions and distances to places you want to go. They are helpful when you are driving somewhere unfamiliar.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always stop completely.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach an unmarked railroad crossing. Look both ways to make sure no trains are coming. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance from the tracks and wait until the train passes before crossing.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct turning lanes?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes are for driving straight or turning.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower and less reliable.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, you should look:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
In your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
In your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A car could be stopped just out of sight. Slow down as you approach hills and curves so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must travel at exactly this speed.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at this speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign showing the maximum speed allowed. During rain, snow, ice, or poor conditions, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have left the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the wheels slightly left to get back on the pavement.
Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, grip the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Let your car slow down, then check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel back suddenly, as this can cause you to lose control or cross into other lanes.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This helps prevent your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When you see this road sign, what should you do?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black letters. This sign shows that a divided highway is starting and you should stay on the right side.

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no visible stop line or crosswalk, where should a driver stop?

options.text: They do not have to stop.
They should slow down to make sure the road is clear.
They should stop where they can see 200 feet on both sides, even if it means entering the intersection.
They should stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest point to the intersection where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.
